N.B.—The Kowloon and Lappa Custom Houses collect Native Tariff Duty on all goods from Hongkong and Macao sent by junks to Chinese Ports not open to Foreign shipping; Native Tariff Duty on goods outwards, i.e., to Hongkong and Macao, whether from open or non-open ports if unprovided with documents proving payment of Export Duty; and Likin at the Provincial rate on such goods inwards or outwards as are liable to Likin. Accordingly, the statistics supplied by the Kowloon and Lappa Custom Houses do not contain complete Returns of the cargoes of junks inwards and outwards, seeing that the cargoes of junks to and from ports open to Foreign shipping, i.e., Treaty Ports, are dealt with by the Native Customs at those ports, and not by the Kowloon and Lappa Customs.

transcriber_notes: Layout: for each country the book prints 'Imports from' and 'Exports to' in the Hk. Tls. column of each year, with the country's combined total printed below them (after a rule) in the 'Total, Hk. Tls.' column. Here the combined total is placed on the country's heading row; the Imports/Exports rows carry the Hk. Tls. figures.
Country names printed in small capitals, each followed by ':—' (dropped here). 'Total Imports' and 'Less Re-exports to Foreign Countries' (p. 164) have figures in the Hk. Tls. columns only.
p. 164: the sub-heading of the first 1926 column is misprinted 'Total,' instead of 'Hk. Tls.'; transcribed under the normal column name.

'—' = nil as printed. Some figures print a semicolon for a comma (Hongkong 1927 imports '212;592,777', total '382;272,655'; British India 1927 imports '42;392,614', total '64;587,433'); transcribed with commas.

Many right-hand digits are clipped at the column rules. Where the surviving part of the glyph was unambiguous (e.g. the waist of an 8, both sides of a 0) it was read; otherwise the cell is left blank (see below).
